title: Correcting a Name With Kindness
script: Lina: [gently] Rafi, can I ask you about something from this morning's meeting?
Rafi: Of course. Did I forget to send you one of the notes?
Lina: No, the notes were clear. It is about our new colleague, Naila. You called her Nadia three times.
Rafi: [surprised] Oh, I did not realize that. The names sounded similar in my head, and nobody corrected me.
Lina: She looked uncomfortable, but she did not want to interrupt you in front of the whole team.
Rafi: [regretfully] I feel terrible. I should have checked her name before I introduced her.
Lina: Mistakes happen. I wanted to tell you privately so you can correct it without feeling embarrassed.
Rafi: Thank you. That was kinder than announcing it across the office.
Lina: What will you do now?
Rafi: I will speak to Naila before lunch. I will say her name correctly, apologize briefly, and not make excuses.
Lina: [calmly] That sounds good. You could also correct the meeting notes because her name appears there twice.
Rafi: You're right. I will update the file and send the corrected version to everyone.
Lina: Do you think I should make a long apology in the group chat?
Rafi: Probably not. A simple correction protects her from more mistakes without making her the center of attention.
Lina: I understand. I want her to know that remembering her name matters.
Rafi: It does. A person's name is a basic part of showing respect.
Lina: [warmly] Thank you for telling me quietly, Lina. You helped both of us today.
Rafi: And thank you for listening calmly. Some people become defensive when they are corrected.
Lina: I was embarrassed for a moment, but the important thing is fixing the mistake.
Rafi: [warmly] Exactly. Kind correction and a sincere response can keep a small error from becoming a bigger problem.
